title: Enforce a typed Git-tree applicability restriction on remote-derived verification evidence
outcome: A remote-derived check minted at a gated checkpoint can carry a typed Git-tree restriction that every evidence-selection route enforces against a host-measured tree on the judged source basis, and no reader silently treats a restricted record as unrestricted
acceptance: ExecutionSourceBasis accepts an optional host-measured git_tree (validated lowercase hex, refused by name otherwise) on checkpoint execution observations and execution_observe sightings; turn_checkpoint.verification_evidence accepts an optional applicability {kind: git_tree, tree} and refuses by name a restriction whose producer observation's source_basis lacks that exact tree; existing records' canonical bytes are unchanged

Every route that selects verification evidence to satisfy a test requirement (obligation satisfaction, completion's newest-check rule, bound-criterion evaluation citation, bound-from and attach) uses one shared predicate: a restricted record qualifies only when the relevant judged sighting carries an equal git_tree; a missing or different tree leaves it attributed but non-qualifying; matching tree with a different commit qualifies

Tests cover: an unused old restricted record does not veto a newer qualifying local check with equal content-v1 and a different tree; a selected restricted record with a mismatched or missing tree does not satisfy; mixed restricted records are each checked against their own restriction; matching tree qualifies
The stored VerificationEvidence reader refuses undeclared members by name (strict), with a pre-commit doctor+readiness census on every live store

A new declared rebuildable projection object, established by the narrow projection step in the agreed cutover, is the durable older-reader barrier: every build since 28b49ef refuses ordinary open of a store holding it with different_build_schema, without mutation; the host protocol advertises the applicability capability only when the open store holds that object, so no restricted record can be minted before the barrier exists; docs record the barrier, the ordering rule and that removing the object once restricted records exist is not allowed

completion.summary: Remote-derived verification evidence can carry a typed Git-tree restriction: an optional host-measured git_tree on the source basis, and an optional applicability {kind: git_tree, tree} on checkpoint evidence. One shared predicate enforces it on every evidence-selection route; the stored reader is strict, and a declared rebuildable projection object is the older-reader barrier. The host advertises the capability only when the barrier exists. Landed in 56f84d7 (full gate test-0c4b836f PASS), pre-commit census on all 6 stores, installed as b96a94ed, and cut over live on 2026-10-29 (barrier 6/6, readiness 6/6). The independent evaluation 45c515b1 passed 5/5.
